{"message":"Hi there,

If your SSO configuration is pointing to an unexpected identity‑provider domain, it’s treated as a potential admin‑level compromise. An admin who still has access should immediately go to **Settings → Security → SSO** and either disable the SSO integration or point it back to the correct provider. After you’ve reverted the setting, please **report the change to support** so a reviewer can check when and how the configuration was altered and which account made the change.

Thanks!"}

arguments.message:
Hi there,

If your SSO configuration is pointing to an unexpected identity‑provider domain, it’s treated as a potential admin‑level compromise. An admin who still has access should immediately go to **Settings → Security → SSO** and either disable the SSO integration or point it back to the correct provider. After you’ve reverted the setting, please **report the change to support** so a reviewer can check when and how the configuration was altered and which account made the change.

While you’re there, also verify that the callback URL shown in **Settings → Security → SSO → Configuration** matches exactly (character for character) the reply/redirect URL configured on the identity‑provider side – even a trailing slash or http/https mismatch can cause redirects to the wrong place.

Let us know once you’ve made the change or if you run into any issues.

Thanks!
